name: Mestanolone

card.summary: An old oral 17-methyl DHT steroid: strongly androgenic, weakly anabolic, mostly discontinued; no modern trials.
card.note: US Schedule III; hepatotoxic like other 17-alkylated steroids.

quick.overview:
Mestanolone is a mid-20th-century oral steroid derived from DHT. It was sold as a medicine but turned out to be mostly androgenic rather than strongly anabolic.

It is largely discontinued, and the literature on it is mostly about detecting it in doping control.
quick.mechanism: It activates the androgen receptor directly and cannot convert to estrogen. The 17-methyl group allows oral activity.
quick.risks: Reported effects include virilisation and liver damage. It is Schedule III in the US and controlled in many other countries.

lead: Mestanolone, also called methylandrostanolone or 17alpha-methyldihydrotestosterone, is a synthetic androgen and anabolic steroid. It is essentially an orally active form of dihydrotestosterone (DHT), the potent androgen that drives male secondary sexual characteristics. It was sold in mid-20th-century medicine under brand names such as Ermalone and Androstalone and is now mostly discontinued, although Wikipedia notes it remains available in Japan.[1]

Anabolic steroids interest people who want more muscle, strength and a more masculine physique. Mestanolone's route to those goals is through the androgen receptor, which it activates strongly. Unlike testosterone, it is not converted to estrogen, and skeletal muscle inactivates it, so it was initially thought to be a strong anabolic agent but later research showed its effects to be mainly androgenic rather than muscle-building.[1]

Published literature is dominated by analytical chemistry: how mestanolone and its metabolites are detected in urine, hair and horse urine for doping control.[3][5][6][7] No modern clinical trial of its effects on muscle or appearance was found.

chain: Binds the androgen receptor as a DHT-like steroid
Strong androgenic effect; weak anabolic effect in muscle
angle.text: Mestanolone acts like DHT that survives oral dosing. Its androgenic effects are strong, and muscle tissue inactivates it, which is why it has been described as a poor muscle builder compared with other anabolic steroids.

infobox: US Schedule III; controlled in many countries

paras: Medical use was limited. Wikipedia reports that it was sold as 25 mg sublingual tablets under the brand name Ermalone.[1] Outside medicine, the drug is a controlled substance, and non-medical use is generally illegal where it is scheduled.[1]

Wikipedia states that East German Olympic athletes used mestanolone in state-sponsored doping in the 1970s and 1980s and says its value was seen more in effects on the central nervous system and neuromuscular function, such as strength, aggression and focus, than in building muscle.[1]

Mestanolone is an agonist of the androgen receptor and is very similar to DHT, differing only by a 17alpha-methyl group. That group makes it active when taken by mouth, unlike DHT itself.[1] Because it is already 5alpha-reduced, it cannot be aromatised to estrogen and has no estrogenic or progestogenic activity.[1]

Skeletal muscle inactivates it through the enzyme 3alpha-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase, a property shared with DHT and mesterolone that Wikipedia associates with weak anabolic effects.[1] Forum users have discussed this enzyme when comparing structural features of steroids.[10]

Mestanolone is a major metabolite of oxymetholone and shares metabolites with methyltestosterone.[1][2][8] Studies of 17alpha-methyl steroids describe epimerisation at the 17 position and the rearrangement of sulfate conjugates in urine, work that supports anti-doping analysis.[3][4] Methods have been developed to detect it in head hair, alongside other steroids,[5] and in the urine of racehorses.[6][8]

Research in cell culture found that mesterolone, mestanolone and methenolone increased mineralocorticoid and decreased adrenal androgen production in human adrenal cells, indicating CYP17A1 dysfunction.[9]

Mestanolone is a synthetic androstane steroid and a 17alpha-alkylated derivative of DHT. Oxymetholone, oxandrolone and stanozolol belong to the same 17alpha-alkyl family, and oxymetholone is prepared from mestanolone.[1]

Wikipedia lists masculinising effects, including acne, increased hair growth, voice changes and higher sex drive, and notes that the drug is hepatotoxic, as with other 17alpha-alkylated steroids.[1] An animal study of methylandrostanolone and fluoxymesterone in rats treated orally for eight weeks found liver enzyme values within normal range in males, an increase in alkaline phosphatase in steroid-treated females, and reduced cytochrome P-450 levels in male liver microsomes.[11]

Mestanolone was first synthesised in 1935. Roussel developed it in the 1950s, and it was marketed under names such as Androstalone and Ermalone by at least 1960. It was initially thought to be a potent anabolic agent before later work showed its effects to be mainly androgenic.[1]
In the United States mestanolone is a Schedule III controlled substance, and it is controlled in many other countries.[1] Anti-doping and racing laboratories treat it as a target compound.[5][6]

Forensic reports show the drug appearing in illicit supply: a 2025 Scottish prison study found mestanolone among steroids in seized tablets and powders between 2019 and 2023, and a 2024 case study identified mestanolone and oxandrolone in five seized e-cigarette cartridges.[12][13] On T Nation, mestanolone appears in lists of banned substances for drug-free competitions and in discussion of designer prohormones and 17-methyl DHT derivatives.[14][15][16]

No studies found of mestanolone as a treatment or for muscle or appearance outcomes in people. Published papers are analytical studies on metabolism and detection,[3][4][5][6][8] a cell-culture profiling study of steroidogenesis,[9] a rat liver study,[11] and forensic seizure reports.[12][13]

timeline.event: Marketed under brand names including Androstalone and Ermalone by about this year.[1]
Reportedly used in East German state-sponsored doping, continuing into the 1980s.[1]
Metabolism studies describe 17-epimerisation of 17alpha-methyl steroids including mestanolone.[3]
Case study reports mestanolone in seized prison e-cigarettes.[13]

lore.intro: On T Nation, mestanolone is mostly mentioned in passing: in banned-substance lists, as a parent structure of designer prohormones, and in discussions of androgenic side effects.[14][15][16][17]

claims.claim: Mestanolone is highly androgenic and hard on the body despite being 'not as harmful' as some steroids.
claims.believers: A T Nation poster discussing kidney strain suggested that a metabolite with very high affinity for the androgen receptor explains why a related steroid is strongly androgenic and that prolonged hypertension can lead to kidney damage.[17]
claims.experts: Wikipedia describes mestanolone as having strong androgenic and weak anabolic effects with liver toxicity; no trial has examined kidney outcomes.[1]

claims.claim: Designer supplements such as Superdrol are derivatives of 17-methyl DHT.
claims.believers: A T Nation thread analysed the label claim of Superdrol and said it would be a 2alpha-methyl derivative of 17-methyl-DHT, or mestanolone, a controlled steroid.[16]
claims.experts: Wikipedia describes mestanolone as a controlled substance in the United States (Schedule III).[1]
